_comment: Research directions. On the home page, each direction's 'short' label becomes a topic tab and its 'summary' is shown under the tabs; research.html lists every direction with its full 'description' (2-4 sentences), 'keywords' and optional 'links' [{label, url}]. 'interests' is the comma-separated 'Research interests' line on the home page. Replace the [[...]] placeholders.

directions.name: Multi-hypothesis visual reasoning
directions.summary: Agents that keep several interpretations of an ambiguous image alive and reason over them, instead of committing to one answer.
directions.description: Scientific images often support more than one reading. I build probabilistic, agentic frameworks that factorize spatial uncertainty into graph-derived ambiguity blocks, propagate it through segmentation and measurement, and keep multiple hypotheses until the evidence separates them.

directions.name: Prompt-response landscapes of foundation models
directions.summary: Mapping how a promptable segmentation model's outputs change with the prompt, and how likely each distinct answer is.
directions.description: A single promptable segmentation model can give very different masks for nearby prompts. I map these prompt-response basins: designing sampling strategies that find the distinct outputs a model can produce and estimate their probability mass under a limited inference budget.

directions.name: Diversity of reasoning in LLMs
directions.summary: Measuring how differently people and LLMs search for solutions on abstract visual reasoning tasks.
directions.description: On ARC-style visual reasoning tasks, humans propose a wide range of candidate rules. Using a new semantic similarity metric and manifold analysis of solution trajectories, I compare that diversity with LLMs and find roughly 2× lower semantic diversity in LLaMA-family models, pointing to limits in adaptive conceptual search.

directions.name: AI for scientific imaging
directions.summary: Reliable, reproducible image analysis for microscopy and robotics, where errors carry real costs.
directions.description: I apply these ideas to real imaging problems: open-source tooling for atomic force microscopy that made cellulose nanocrystal measurement faster and more reproducible across labs, and perception for agricultural robots that pick deformable objects.
